findings.location: report phase-10 section (Bridge comparison paragraph) vs lib/benchmark-history.mjs crossVersionEstimates/datedEstimates
findings.evidence: Report states all 60 real estimates were bridged 'via bridge-median-ratio with 8 bridges' and the UI proof shows a badge 'relative estimate · 8 bridge models · ±17% bridge spread', while the frozen before/after evidence for the same benchmark bridge (aa-coding-agent-index::1.4 -> ::1.5) reports 'bridge_count': 67 for the dated-state estimate of aa-coding:1.4:0 and the report's own before/after paragraph cites 67 bridges. These cannot both be correct for the same family pair; the '8 bridges' figure is not derivable from any supplied artifact and is contradicted by the owner's own controlled-experiment JSON.
findings.repair: Reconcile the bridge-count claim in the report and UI evidence: state per-path bridge counts explicitly (cross-version path vs dated-state path) and correct whichever of '8' / '67' is wrong, citing the exact estimate record ids. Do not publish both numbers unqualified.

findings.evidence: SCHEMA.md says the 'historical' object exists 'once at least one dated state exists', but the real dataset facts show historical.states.length = 1 and 60 live cross-version estimates — so estimates are produced even with only one state, and the mechanism is not inert. Conversely the same doc's Limitations section says 'Dated-state estimates only exist once a second, distinct state has been retained — the mechanism is inert on a single state', conflating the dated-state path (correct) with the whole historical mechanism (incorrect).
findings.repair: Rewrite the two SCHEMA.md sentences to say: cross-version estimates are produced once the registry has ≥2 versions of a family in the current observations; dated-state estimates additionally require ≥2 distinct retained states; with a single state only the cross-version path is live.

findings.location: lib/benchmark-history.mjs computeRankShift (C4/C7 boundary) and SCHEMA.md 'Special cases'
findings.evidence: computeRankShift gates on 'iqr_relative = iqr' against the 0–1 rank scale and documents that in code and docs, so the ±25% gate on rank shifts is a different (scale-relative, not median-relative) quantity than the ratio gate, but both are described in SCHEMA.md and the report under the single phrase 'the same ±25 % IQR gate applies'. The gate is the same threshold, not the same relative measure; a reader may wrongly infer the rank gate is 25% of the median shift (and when shift median is 0, as in the synthetic test, iqr_relative equals absolute IQR).
findings.repair: Add one sentence to SCHEMA.md and the report: for rank shifts the 25% limit is applied to the absolute IQR on the 0–1 rank scale (iqr_relative = iqr there), not to an IQR-relative-to-median as for ratios.

findings.evidence: If a source/pairs value is not found in oldSorted (rankIn returns 1 for a missing value, i.e. last place), the shift is silently computed against a fabricated rank instead of refusing the bridge. In the frozen call paths the pairs are derived from the same maps as oldValues/newValues, so this is not reachable in current wiring, but the exported helper is permissive.
findings.repair: Either document rankIn's missing-value convention at the export site or make computeRankShift drop pairs whose old_value/new_value is absent from the respective sorted boards, so the public API cannot produce a shift from a non-existent rank.
